item.title: Brazil: The craze for candidate merch ahead of elections
item.description: Nearly 159 million Brazilians will head to the polling booths on Sunday to vote in general elections. They will elect their new MPs, see two-thirds of the Senate change ranks and, most importantly, vote for their next president.Though the vote is held by secret ballot, people wear their support on their sleeve. Candidates and parties are brandished on flags throughout the streets of #RiodeJaneiro, and business is booming for vendors selling merchandise for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro.FRANCE 24's Brazil correspondent Jan Onoszko brings you this report. item.title: ¿Puede la inteligencia artificial amenazar la creación literaria?
item.description: La Academia Goncourt ha retirado de sus candidaturas una novela del escritor Thélyson Orélien tras las sospechas de que fue redactada con inteligencia artificial. El autor niega las imputaciones y defiende que el estilo de su obra refleja la tradición oral caribeña. La decisión reabre el debate sobre los límites de la inteligencia artificial en la creación artística, la autoría y los criterios para distinguir una obra humana de un texto generado por máquinas. ¿Cómo puede el mundo literario afrontar este desafío sin prejuzgar a los autores? Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: As Europe's balance of power shifts eastward, France & Spain seek to 'reinforce their own positions'
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Carlos Mascarell Vilar, political scientist based in Spain. From his own perspective, Emmanuel Macron's visit to Spain needs to be understood by European power, political legacy, and geoeconomics. France and Spain are seeking to reinforce their bilateral relationship at a moment when the balance of power within Europe is changing rapidly, particularly with the growing importance of countries in the east such as Poland. For Macron, strengthening the Madrid-Paris axis is also part of a broader effort to advance European defence and strategic sovereignty. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Matisse comes to Amsterdam in major new show
item.description: From the October 3 visitors to Amsterdam's H'ART museum will be able to see an extensive collection of works by artist Henri Matisse alongside pieces inspired by his legacy, including Mark Rothko, Barnett Newman, and Pablo Picasso. The new exhibition was organised in collaboration with the Pompidou Centre in Paris. Fuente: France 24 - English.
